newsitem.title: INDIA: Three Australian wheat shipments arrive in India.
newsitem.headline: Three Australian wheat shipments arrive in India.

text.p: Three ships carrying over 83,000 tonnes of Australian wheat have reached Indian ports, an Indian government statement said on Tuesday.
The statement said the Doric Chariot, a vessel carrying about 60,000 tonnes wheat, had landed at Jawahar Lal Nehru Port near Bombay.
Two other vessels had berthed last week, one at Vishakapatnam in the southern state of Andhra Pradesh and the other at New Mangalore in the southern state of Karnataka, the statement said.
Two other vessels with about 69,700 tonnes of wheat would arrive in India by the end of January, it said.
The government had so far chartered 27 vessels for wheat, including five from Canada and 22 from Australia, the statement said.
"These vessels would bring about 900,000 tonnes of wheat by the end of March 1997," it said.
The Indian government in December authorised the state-run State Trading Corp (STC) to import two million tonnes of wheat to augment supplies and check rising domestic prices.
STC officials said they had so far contracted to import 1.25 million tonnes of wheat.
